inductive BDir where
  | left  : BDir   -- B₁ branch
  | mid   : BDir   -- B₂ branch
  | right : BDir   -- B₃ branch
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

/-- A position in the Berggren tree is a finite word over {left, mid, right}. -/
abbrev BPos := List BDir

/-- Apply a single Berggren step. -/
def berggrenStep (d : BDir) (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ :=
  let (a, b, c) := t
  match d with
  | .left  => (a - 2*b + 2*c, 2*a - b + 2*c, 2*a - 2*b + 3*c)
  | .mid   => (a + 2*b + 2*c, 2*a + b + 2*c, 2*a + 2*b + 3*c)
  | .right => (-a + 2*b + 2*c, -2*a + b + 2*c, -2*a + 2*b + 3*c)

/-- The Pythagorean triple at a given position (path applied left-to-right from root). -/
def berggrenAt (path : BPos) : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ :=
  path.foldl (fun t d => berggrenStep d t) (3, 4, 5)

/-- Each Berggren step preserves the Pythagorean equation. -/
theorem berggrenStep_preserves_pyth (d : BDir) (a b c : ℤ)

  cases d <;> simp [berggrenStep] <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a - b), sq_nonneg (a + b)]

concept.title: Closure systems as tropical idempotent semimodules via finite max-plus support functions
concept.concept_description: The key insight is that a finite closure operator can be encoded by its family of closed sets as a max-plus support function, turning closure-theoretic reconstruction into a tropical/idempotent linear object and yielding concrete order-preserving algorithms for recovering closures from probe data. Why now: the catalog already contains strong closure infrastructure in `Bridges/AlgebraEMLClosureComputation.lean`, `Bridges/AlgebraEMLReconstruction.lean`, and thermodynamic finite-closure machinery in `Bridges/AlgebraicEMLThermodynamicFormalism.lean`, while Tropical has a live but still incomplete canonical layer in `Tropical/Canonical/Basic.lean`; this makes a new cross-domain theorem feasible without repeating the in-flight tropical Jacobian work. Concretely, for a finite type α and closure operator cl on `Set α`, define for each subset S a tropical indicator/support function on `{0,1}^α` or equivalently on finitely supported weight vectors by taking the max-plus score of membership in closed supersets. Prove that the resulting family is monotone, idempotent under tropical addition/max, and separates points exactly when the original closure system is reconstructible from probes. Then establish an equivalence theorem: finite closure-stable probe families correspond to finitely generated tropical semimodules of support functions satisfying a closure-idempotence axiom. A second target is algorithmic: given a finite probe family, construct the least closure operator compatible with the probes and prove that its closed sets are exactly the tropical halfspace intersections determined by those support functions. This would create a genuine Algebra/EML/Tropical bridge inside Bridges, produce computable reconstruction pipelines rather than isolated lemmas, and could fail in interesting ways if finite-generation or separation hypotheses are too weak.
